(I saw <@199561711278227457> was typing lol) The test vector generation is already a CI job, its just scoped to manual run. I can make it nightly if there's a wish for that. I wouldn't make it a release, but it should be easy to target the artifact of the last CI scheduled job and pull the vectors from there. e.g: grep all CI runs of a certain workflow, then pick latest of that and pull artefact? haha, basically the same thought as hww 😄 alternatively, I can push it to an s3 bucket and label it with a timestamp if thats easier Any eta for the testvectors including Lucas's PR? Will there be a new release this week? I'll try to rebase my ePBS work on top of that, but have my local Python testing environment broken I don't know why If I have 10 consolidations from validator 1...10 and the target validator is always validator 11, all 10 consolidation requests are sent in 10 separate transactions included in 1 block. Assuming everything is above board (gas, etc all good), then is the expected behaviour that we see 10 consolidations show up as consolidation requests in the next slot? Or will i see the next slot with consolidation 1->11, then the slot after will have consolidation 2->11 and so on until 10->11, i.e, it takes 10 slots to pass these consolidations as a consolidation request in the slot? I hope it will be in next week before ACDC (🤞) https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3920 each block contains one consolidation request. The requests are queued in the consolidation contract on EL side, each new block grabs one consolidation request from the queue.

excerpts.content:
we thought about it but currently we don't have an explicit approach to verify if the test vectors are all generated without errors.

I think we would not provide nightly build results (tarball files) on github release pages. wonder if there is other storage methods for that. *And* if it's okay that the nightly build tarballs *are not verified at some confidence level*.

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content: The test vector generation is already a CI job, its just scoped to manual run. I can make it nightly if there's a wish for that. I wouldn't make it a release, but it should be easy to target the artifact of the last CI scheduled job and pull the vectors from there. e.g: grep all CI runs of a certain workflow, then pick latest of that and pull artefact?
